title: Torin 1 vs DMSO from 'treatment', 4 + 4 Ribo-seq/RNA-seq pairs, 3,174 genes tested
summary: 2,000,000 reads per library were subsampled from ENA; rRNA took 56%–87% of the Ribo-seq reads and 4%–26% of all reads aligned to the one-transcript-per-gene transcriptome.

Three-nucleotide periodicity (share of P-sites in frame 0 within CDSs) per Ribo-seq library: GSM3889077 0.45, GSM3889078 0.43, GSM3889085 0.44, GSM3889086 0.45, GSM3889079 0.42, GSM3889080 0.43, GSM3889087 0.46, GSM3889088 0.46.
Torin 1 versus DMSO ('treatment'): 4 Ribo-seq/RNA-seq pairs against 4, 3,174 genes tested of 19,857 counted.

At padj < 0.05, 23 genes are translationally regulated (ΔTE changes while the mRNA does not), 0 are buffered, 1 change transcriptionally with the ribosomes following the mRNA, 0 are intensified and 3,150 are unchanged.
ΔTE falls in 21 genes and rises in 2.
The translationally regulated genes with the smallest ΔTE adjusted p-values are GAPDH, PABPC1, YBX1, HSPA8, VIM, CCT2, CSDE1, HNRNPDL.

figures.title: Metagene
figures.caption: P-site coverage around start and stop codons, pooled over 8 Ribo-seq libraries, coloured by reading frame; periodicity per library GSM3889077 0.45, GSM3889078 0.43, GSM3889085 0.44, GSM3889086 0.45, GSM3889079 0.42, GSM3889080 0.43, GSM3889087 0.46, GSM3889088 0.46.

figures.title: Footprint lengths
figures.caption: Read-length distribution after trimming per Ribo-seq library; modal lengths GSM3889077 32 nt, GSM3889078 32 nt, GSM3889085 33 nt, GSM3889086 31 nt, GSM3889079 32 nt, GSM3889080 32 nt, GSM3889087 32 nt, GSM3889088 31 nt.

figures.title: ΔTE
figures.caption: Δ RNA against Δ Ribo (log2 fold change, Torin 1 vs DMSO) for 3,174 genes; 23 translationally regulated, 0 buffered, 1 transcriptional, 0 intensified at padj < 0.05; the dashed line is Δ Ribo = Δ RNA.

warnings: The laptop tier is a lower-fidelity approximation of nf-core/riboseq: reads were subsampled, aligned with bowtie2 to one GENCODE transcript per gene (no genome alignment, no splice-aware mapping, no multi-isoform handling), and P-site offsets came from a simple mode rule rather than riboWaltz or a trained model.
'genotype/variation' takes 2 values among the chosen libraries (sgLARP1, wild-type); the contrast pools them.

4 libraries (GSM3889081, GSM3889082, GSM3889083, GSM3889084) had more than half of their reads match neither rRNA nor a protein-coding transcript; such reads are usually other non-coding RNA (tRNA, snoRNA) that the one-transcript-per-gene reference does not hold, so the counts rest on the smaller mRNA fraction.
